hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Count live FP values at the target's `@0x150 fmuls f0,f12,f31` from the fnasm dump alone, zero builds: if that count is 14 or fewer, the pressure story is wrong and the f31 comes from something other than the volatile bank being full, so no amount of adding locals will produce it. If instead the count is 15, the same census on OUR dump at `@0x148 fmuls f0,f11,f10` names exactly which value we are missing.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no -- every instruction quoted above is read from the target's own dump and is accurate, but the live-FP census itself was NOT run, and the `camera->viewport[3][0]` local was never probed. Note the pad is NOT the lever: the slot map from probe.py shows target and ours agreeing on every slot at 4,16,20,24,64,68,72,76,80,84,88,92,96,100,104,108,116 and differing ONLY at 128/132/136/140, which is precisely the 8-byte f31 home plus the displaced LR reload, so `u8 unused[16]` is already correctly sized.
hypothesis.statement: The residual is ONE callee-saved FPR and nothing else, and the missing value is a fifteenth simultaneously-live FP quantity rather than a mis-scheduled load. Read off `fnasm.py game/mb/mb_camera.c MBWorldToScreen3D`: the target's prologue carries `@0xc stfd f31,128(r1)` and its epilogue `@0x190 lfd f31,128(r1)`, and f31 has exactly one definition and one consumer in the whole body -- `@0x13c lfs f31,212(r10)` (that is camera->viewport[1][1], our `yDenomB`) consumed at `@0x150 fmuls f0,f12,f31`, whose other operand is defined `@0x140 lfs f12,148(r10)` (camera->projection[1][1], our `yDenomA`). Our stream computes the identical product with two VOLATILE registers, `@0x128 lfs f10,212(r10)` and `@0x12c lfs f11,148(r10)` consumed at `@0x148 fmuls f0,f11,f10`, and the operand ORDER already agrees. MWCC only reaches f31 when f0-f13 are all occupied, so the target is holding one more live FP value across that point than we are, and the next lane should find the value we are NOT keeping alive rather than trying to move the ones we are. The prime candidate is a local for `camera->viewport[3][0]`, which the target loads at `@0x10c lfs f4,240(r10)` and does not consume until `@0x14c fnmsubs f2,f11,f4,f2` -- a 16-instruction live range our source spells inline inside `xNumerator -= projected[2] * camera->viewport[3][0]` while every one of its three siblings at 212/244/148 already has a named local.
